Subject: Suncrest RFP - DPF / DPA Annex clarifications

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the materials so far — Suncrest is working through the security/compliance annex in our RFP (Appendix B) and we have a handful of specific clarifications we need before the procurement committee signs off. Can you please provide concise answers to the items below and attach any evidence you can share? We're on a tight schedule and would appreciate responses by EOD Thursday.

1) Cross-border transfers: For EU personal data processed by Redwood, list the processing locations (cloud regions / on-prem options) and the legal transfer mechanism(s) you rely on (SCCs, UK Addendum, DPF equivalence, etc.).
2) DPA Annex: Do you offer a customer-redlined DPA annex or only your standard annex? Please indicate if you support controller-to-controller or controller-to-processor wording.
3) KMS / key custody: What KMS integrations are supported? Can customers supply their own keys / HSM?
4) Runtime & caching: Do you persist KV cache, embeddings, or other derived artifacts? If so, what is default retention and can it be disabled? Are cached tokens stored outside the customer region?
5) Technical evidence: We need the latest SOC 2 Type II report (covering inference/runtime), pen test summary, and network flow diagram. Redact sensitive IP as needed.

I've attached Appendix B for reference. If any of the asks are best addressed in a short technical call, propose times and we can book.

Best,
Eleanor Brandt
Senior Procurement Manager
Suncrest Health

Hi Eleanor — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (security/ops) and Karthik (privacy & legal support) so we can provide a consolidated response and share supporting artifacts.

High-level: we can meet your timeline. We've attached a one-page Redwood_DPF_Summary that maps your asks to the evidence we'll share. Below are short answers to get you started; Kimberly/Karthik will follow up with the technical annex and the SOC2 redacted report.

1) Cross-border transfers: EU customer data is processed primarily in GCP europe-west6 and our EU dedicated private option (VPC-based) can be deployed on-prem or in customer-managed cloud accounts. We rely on SCCs with a standard DPA annex; for customers requiring a controller-to-controller contract we can discuss a tailored annex.

2) DPA Annex: We provide a Redwood standard DPA with an annex for data transfers and subprocessors. We accept customer redlines; for larger enterprise customers we typically execute a mutually negotiated annex.

3) KMS / key custody: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own-key via customer-managed HSMs for our Private deployments. For Hosted customers we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys where contractually agreed.

4) Runtime & caching: Default KV cache is transient and optimized for latency; by default cache entries are held for up to 72 hours and are encrypted at rest. Embeddings are not stored persistently under the default Hosted setting; persistent embeddings/feature stores are opt-in and must be explicitly enabled by the customer. All cache persistence can be disabled for privacy-sensitive workloads.

5) Technical evidence: Kimberly will attach SOC 2 Type II summary and the redacted pentest report. We can provide a network flow diagram and a DPA annex draft for your legal team.

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute deep-dive tomorrow morning (CT) or Friday. Proposed times: Thu 9:00–11:00 CT or Fri 14:00–16:00 CT.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Eleanor / Naomi — adding the technical details requested below. I'm attaching the draft DPA annex (dpa_annex_suncrest_v3.docx) and a redacted SOC2. Highlights / clarifications:

- Processing footprint: EU inference and data plane operations run in GCP europe-west6 by default for EU tenants. For Private deployments we support deployment into customer VPCs in EU regions or on-prem (air-gapped packaging available for high-regulated workloads).

- Transfer mechanism: Our standard approach for EU→non-EU transfers is execution of the EU SCCs (2021 module 2/3) embedded in our DPA annex. For customers requiring additional assurances we can include contractual safeguards (e.g., UK Addendum) and document technical mitigations in the DPF. We do not rely solely on adequacy decisions for high-risk transfers.

- KMS/HSM: Supported integrations: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault for envelope encryption. For Dedicated/Private we support customer-supplied HSMs (PKCS#11) and can integrate a customer-managed key rotation schedule. When customer keys are in-use, Redwood has no access to plaintext model inputs/outputs at rest.

- Runtime caching & persistence:
  • KV cache: in-memory primary; fallback disk-backed cache is encrypted and configured with a default 72-hour TTL.
  • Embeddings: Hosted mode — embeddings are ephemeral unless customer explicitly enables a persistent embedding store. Persistent stores are region-bound to the customer's selected region and subject to retention settings.
  • Logs & telemetry: Request metadata (token counts, latency) are retained for 90 days by default for observability; full request payloads are not retained unless customer opts-in for debugging or audit purposes.

- Network & attestations: Redacted SOC 2 Type II attached. Pen test summary attached (no customer-identifying details). Network diagram: inference control plane communicates with model GPU hosts over private peering; egress to public internet is tightly restricted and logged.

Next steps: Naomi / Karthik — recommend we share the attachments, propose a 30-minute technical call to walk procurement/legal through the DPA annex, and offer a short demo of the Private deployment flow. Eleanor — if you share a preferred slot we will confirm.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Eleanor — quick legal/privacy clarifications inline:

1) DPA redlines: We accept redlines and prefer to track changes in the docx annex; our legal team usually closes commercial DPA negotiations within 2–3 business days for standard asks.

2) Controller/Processor: Redwood acts as processor for customers using Hosted or Dedicated inference; for specific joint-processing integrations (rare) we can discuss controller-to-controller wording. We have included a short note in the annex describing typical processor commitments.

3) Routing & fallback: Our routing policy can pin customer traffic to EU-only model variants and regions. For resilience we support automatic fallback to compatible model variants in another EU region; we will not route EU-tagged customer traffic to non-EU regions unless explicitly configured by the customer (or in an emergency with documented escalation).

4) Embeddings persistence: Confirming Naomi — embeddings are not persisted by default. If a customer enables a persistent store, we ensure the store is provisioned in the selected region and controlled by customer-configured retention.

I'll be on the call if you'd like to schedule one — Thu 10:00 CT still works for me.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
